title: Advanced Inorganic Chemistry
description: Electronic structure of atoms and molecules. Models for bonding in molecules of nontransition and transition elements. Applications of symmetry to bonding, electronic and vibrational spectroscopy. Stereochemistry of transition metal complexes and introduction to organo- metallics.
prerequisites_raw: Consent of the chemistry graduate advisor.

title: Advanced Inorganic Chemistry
description: Structures of ordered crystalline solids, x-ray crystallography. Introduction to solid state chemistry, inorganic materials and chemical catalysis. Bioinorganic chemistry.
prerequisites_raw: Consent of the chemistry graduate advisor.

title: Graduate Seminar in Inorganic/Analytical Chemistry
description: Seminars on current research topics in inorganic/analytical chemistry presented by faculty, visiting scholars, and postdoctoral and senior graduate students.

title: Bioinorganic Chemistry
description: Selected topics in bioinorganic chemistry and metal-lobiochemistry with a major focus on recent developments. Topics will include discussions of metalloproteins and corresponding model compound investigations. Emphasis will be on reaction mechanisms and spectroscopic properties of metal sites.

title: Synthesis and Properties of Macromolecules
description: Basics of preparation of polymer and macromolecular assemblies, and characterization of large molecules and assemblies. Discussion of chemical structure, bonding, and reactivity.

title: Reaction Mechanisms in Organometallic and Inorganic Chemistry
description: Discussion of chemical reaction mechanisms. Emphasis will be on fundamental reactions of metal compounds such as substitution, addition, elimination, and redox reactions for homogenous catalysis mechanisms and other complex systems.

title: Structural Inorganic Chemistry
description: The use of x-ray and neutron scattering to characterize solid state materials. Subjects include the crystal unit cell, space groups, structure determination and refinement. It is recommended that the student have an elementary introduction to vectors, matrices and fourier series.

title: Solid State Inorganic/Materials
description: An introductory course describing the synthesis, physical characterization, structure, electronic properties and uses of solid state materials.

title: Physical-Inorganic Chemistry
description: Bonding theory, thermodynamics, and structure of inorganic compounds. Applications of physical techniques to the study of inorganic (and organometallic) reactions and their mechanisms.

title: Photochemical and Photophysical Properties of Inorganic and Organometallic Compounds and Materials
description: Discussion of the mechanics of fundamental physical and chemical events which follow absorption of light by inorganic or organometallic chromophores. Consideration of homogeneous and heterogeneous systems as well as the design and operation of photo-optical and photoelectrical devices.

title: Introduction to Inorganic Materials
description: Structures of inorganic materials: close-packing, linking of simple polyhedra. Factors that control structure: ionic radii, covalency, ligand field effects, metal-metal bonding, electron/ atom ratios. Structure-property relationships in e.g. spinels, garnets, perovskites, rutiles, flourites, zeolites, b-aluminas, graphites, common inorganic glasses.

title: Selected Topics in Inorganic Chemistry
description: This course is designed to reflect recent developments in inorganic chemistry.

title: Nuclear and Radiochemistry
description: Radioactive decay kinetics and energetics, nuclear models, nuclear reactions, radiation detection, radiochemical techniques, and applications of radioactivity.

title: Sustainability (with a Chemistry Emphasis)
description: This course will address and identify a number of issues in sustainability that are challenging a sustainable world and the potential research and technical opportunities for addressing these. Topics include: Climate Change—causes and effects; Environmental Monitoring; Energy – production and storage; Chemical resources - challenges and solutions; Recycling; Sustainable Materials; Research and Development Opportunities; Intellectual Property and Innovation.

title: Protein Crystallography
description: Introduction to diffraction techniques. protein crystal growth and morphology. Data collection and reduction strategies. Approaches for solving the phase problem. Crystallographic refinement, including molecular dynamics. Interpretation of crystal structures.

title: Synthesis and Bonding of Small Conjugated Molecules
description: Examination of small organic molecules used in optoelectronic devices: film transistors; light emitting diodes and solar cells. Methods for their synthesis. Influence of molecular structure on energies of molecular orbitals. Development of structure/function relationships based on solid state arrangements.

title: Organic Semiconductors for Energy Conversion
description: Basic photophysics of organic semiconductors. Examination of energy level alignments and solid state arrangements required for the conversion of solar energy into useful electrical energy. Important device considerations for evaluating power conversion efficiencies. Comparison of different solar conversion technologies.

title: Instrumental Methods in Materials Chemistry
description: Principles and practice of advanced research instrumentation for soft materials characterization including spectroscopy, microscopy, and X-ray techniques

title: Chemical Literature
description: Lectures and exercises on the literature and other information resources of use in chemistry.

title: Synthetic Chemistry of Macromolecules
description: Molecular architecture and classifica tion of macromolecules. Different methods for the preparation of polymers: free radical polymerization, ionicpolymerization, condensation polymerization and coordination polymerization. bulk, solution, and emulsion polymerization. Principles of copolymerization, blockcopolymerization, grafting, network formation, chemical reactions on polymers.

title: Organometallic Chemistry: Structure, Bonding, and Applications
description: Synthesis, structure, and reactivity of organometallic complexes, with an emphasis on bonding and electronic structure. Homogeneous catalysis and small molecule activation, especially in the context of the energy conversion and storage, will also be discussed. Graduate students will be required to demonstrate a deeper understanding of the course material during class discussions and in submitted work. Graduate students will additionally be graded separately on all course work, including exams.

title: Seminar in Chemistry and Biochemistry
description: Presentation of seminar required of all departmental graduate students.

title: Special Seminar in Chemistry
description: Specialized seminar topics.

title: Faculty Research Seminar
description: A series of seminars by departmental faculty describ ing their active research projects.

title: Techniques of Teaching
description: Weekly discussion to cover topics concerning class management, student engagement, supervising experiments and safety (if applicable), leading discussions, advising, and grading.

title: Techniques of Teaching and Laboratory Class Supervision
description: An initial two-three day workshop is followed by weekly discussion. Topics covered: laboratory organization, supervising experiments, safety, presentations, leading discussions, writing quizzes, advising, and grading. Aimed at new teaching assistants.

title: Techniques of Teaching and Laboratory Class Supervision
description: An initial two-three day workshop is followed by weekly discussion. Topics covered: laboratory organization, supervising experiments, safety, presentations, leading discussions, writing quizzes, advising, and grading. Aimed at new teaching assistants.

title: Organic Chemistry Techniques of Teaching and Laboratory Class Supervision
description: Weekly discussion to cover topics concerning class management, student engagement, supervising experiments and safety, leading discussions, advising, and grading in the organic chemistry laboratory.

title: Organic Chemistry Techniques of Teaching and Laboratory Class Supervision
description: An initial two-three day workshop is followed by weekly discussion. Topics covered: laboratory organization, supervising experiments, safety, presentations, leading discussions, writing quizzes, advising, and grading. Aimed at new teaching assistants in Organic Chemistry.
